title: Production GPU OOMs from fragmented allocator + session-store eviction race (hosted/dedicated/private)
creator: Olivia Chen
description: Multiple customers (hosted app, one Dedicated tenant, and a Private on-prem deployment) reported sudden GPU OOMs and degraded throughput over a 48h window. Symptoms pointed to growth in resident device memory despite steady request volume. Correlated traces showed long-tail increases in allocator fragmentation and session-store entries not reclaimed after evictions. This ticket tracks the diagnostic work, the interim mitigations, the runtime patch (safe reclamation and eviction serialization), and customer communications.
timeline_updates: 2025-02-14 - Alert: SE oncall notified after hosted customer reported 30% increase in 95th percentile latency and GPU OOMs in one region.
2025-02-14 - Triage: Assigned to Marcus Lee. Initial mitigation: increase host-side retry/backoff for affected route and bounce a small set of nodes in the pool.
2025-02-15 - Observability: Memory histograms showed rising free-slab counts and growing arena fragmentation; session-store key counts increased without matching KV hits.

2025-02-16 - Reproduction: Test harness replayed production traces and reproduced progressive memory growth on identical model and batch-size using stress harness. Heap profiling captured many small device allocations and scattered free blocks.

2025-02-17 - Root cause hypothesis: concurrent eviction path occasionally races with background compaction; stale references prevent arena free and trigger device-side fragmentation leading to OOM under sustained load.

2025-02-18 - Patch development: Implemented per-session reference accounting and moved compaction to a safe-point where in-flight requests are synchronized for the eviction queue. Added a fast-path for small-block coalescing.
2025-02-20 - Canary rollout: Deployed patch to a small hosted pool and one Dedicated zone. No OOMs observed in canary under replay; throughput stable.
2025-02-21 - Rollout: Gradual rollout to remaining nodes; private customer scheduled for coordinated upgrade 2025-02-24.
2025-02-22 - Follow-ups: Scheduling postmortem and additional observability (alloc origin tagging).
reproduction_steps: 1) Use trace replayer with customer's request mix (content and sequence lengths) at sustained QPS for 6+ minutes.
2) Configure runtime to use same allocator thresholds as affected clusters (small-block threshold lowered).
3) Observe device memory: fragmentation grows even when total logical allocations ~steady.
4) Enable session-store debug logging to see evicted keys lingering for multiple seconds after eviction event.
5) Run heap profile (cuda-memcheck optional) and capture slab distribution.
mitigation_steps: Short-term (within hours): - Increase transient capacity on impacted pools, bump per-customer burst capacity to avoid immediate OOM. - Apply node bounce for worst affected hosts to clear fragmentation. - For Dedicated/Private customers, recommend temporarily lowering max concurrency per process.
Medium-term (days): - Canary rollout of the patch that adds safe-point for compaction and per-session refcounts. - Add alert rule for ‘session-store evicted-not-freed > 5s’ to catch regressions.

Long-term (1+ sprints): - Rework allocator to use segregated free-lists with periodic cooperative defragmentation. - Add alloc origin labels and tokenized tracing to map allocations back to routes/requests.
root_cause_summary: A race between the session-store eviction worker and the allocator's background compaction path allowed stale references to persist for ranges of memory. Those stale references prevented free-list coalescing, causing small-block fragmentation on device memory. Under sustained workload the fragmentation caused effective usable memory to decrease and triggered GPU OOMs. Contributing factors: a) edge-case in eviction code that deferred pointer nulling until after compaction, b) allocator's compaction assumed short-lived hold times, and c) insufficient observability to tie allocations to request origins.
fix_summary: Patch introduces: 1) per-session reference counters that ensure eviction can't retire a buffer until refcount is zero, 2) a compaction safe-point that requires eviction queue synchronization before coalescing free blocks, and 3) a small-block coalescer fast-path to reduce fragmentation. Additionally, telemetry was extended to include allocation origin tags and eviction latency metrics.
patch_pr_links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123 - allocator: add safe-point compaction & session refcounts
https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5131 - telemetry: alloc-origin tagging and eviction metrics
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Canary: Deploy to two small hosted pools and one Dedicated zone; run synthetic trace replays and monitor for 72h.
Phase 1 - Gradual: If canary stable, expand to 30% of capacity over next 24h with automated rollback on increased OOM rate.
Phase 2 - Full: Complete rollout to hosted, then schedule Private customer upgrades with pre-checklist and a rollback image.
Rollback plan: Keep previous runtime image in pool for immediate failover; use container-level switch to route traffic away from patched nodes if issues detected.
qa_and_verification: Test harness: end-to-end replay for multiple customers with different token distributions; verify no progressive fragmentation over 10-minute runs.
Unit tests: added coverage for session refcount edge cases and compaction ordering.
Load tests: ramp to 2x production QPS for 30m in canary before expanding.
Observability: dashboards updated - eviction-lag, alloc-origin heatmap, small-block-fragmentation ratio; set alert thresholds.
postmortem_actions: 1) Postmortem doc (confluence) with timeline and teach-back session scheduled (2025-03-03).
2) Create follow-up ticket to prototype segregated free-lists and cooperative defrag (ENG-32001).
3) Improve runbook: include step to trigger node bounce and temporary concurrency cap when eviction-lag > 5s.
4) Add integration tests to CI that run a short allocator stress scenario to detect regressions.
